legend_note: Higher is more habitable in 2050 (+2.7 °C). Eleven indicators in six equal categories — heat, wildfire, drought and clay, floods, coast, lack of services — each scored 0–100 on its own scale, and the score is 100 minus their average. Open-ended indicators rise on a curve that is half exposed at a declared value (20 tropical nights, 5 days at 35 °C, 2 large fires per 1,000 km² per decade), so a commune's score does not depend on the rest of France. Median commune 63; the Aude and Roussillon coast is lowest, inland Normandy, Picardy and Artois highest. Method after Projet Celsius, which scores positions instead (see the positional layer); wildfire is a model calibrated on observed fires. Click a commune for the six categories.
